transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... I suppose I came in because I had an incident at work that didn’t sit right with me. I was on a board call, and someone asked a small question about the facility budget, nothing major, really, and I just... snapped at them. More sharply than I should have.

That’s not how I run my company, and it’s not how I treat people. I’m not usually like that, so I thought I should talk to someone before it becomes a bigger issue.
Has this kind of reaction—snapping or losing control—happened in other situations, or was this the first time?

As far as I can tell, that board call was the first real instance where I actually snapped like that. It was just a small question about the facility budget, and I reacted too sharply. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but it bothered me because that’s not how I run things or how I treat people.
Since that incident on the board call, have you noticed yourself becoming more irritable or having difficulty managing your emotions in other situations?

I wouldn’t say it’s been happening all over the place, no. The main thing is still that board call… I snapped over a small question about the facility budget, and that’s what bothered me. It felt out of character for me. I try to run my company with more respect than that, so even if it was just one moment, it didn’t sit right with me.
In the time leading up to that board call, have you noticed any changes in your mood, like feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

I wouldn’t say I’m hopeless or anything like that, no. It’s more… things that usually help settle me just aren’t landing the same. A chess problem, going over my hiking notes, even dinner with my wife — I know those are things I normally enjoy, and I should feel something from them, but right now they just feel kind of flat.

I don’t mean to overstate it. It’s just noticeable enough that I’ve wondered if something’s off.
Would you say that you’re not getting as much pleasure or satisfaction from those activities as you used to, or is it more just a background kind of flatness without them feeling different?

I think it’s more that I’m not getting the same satisfaction from them, yes… though I don’t want to make it sound dramatic.

Like, I’ll sit with a chess problem or look over my hiking notes, and normally that settles me. Dinner with my wife, same thing — that should feel good. But lately it’s just kind of flat, like I know I ought to enjoy it and I can’t quite get there. Does that make sense?
Would you say that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in those activities entirely, or is it more that you just don’t get as much out of them as you used to?

More the second one, I think. I haven’t lost interest entirely — I still sit down with the chess problems, I still look at my hiking notes, I still have dinner with my wife.

It’s just… I don’t get as much out of it. Those things usually settle me, and right now they feel flat. Like I know I should enjoy them, but I can’t quite get there. If that’s the right way to put it.
Have you been feeling down or experiencing a loss of pleasure in most activities for most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two weeks or more?

I don’t think it’s been most of the day, nearly every day for two weeks, no. At least… I wouldn’t want to say that if that’s not quite right.

It’s more that right now, the things that usually settle me — a chess problem, my hiking notes, dinner with my wife — they just feel flat. I know I should be enjoying them, but I can’t quite get there. That’s the main thing I’ve noticed.
Over the past two weeks, have you had days where you felt down or where activities didn’t bring you pleasure for most of the day, on most days?

Not for most of the day on most days, I don’t think. I don’t want to overstate it.

It’s more that when I try the things that usually help — a chess problem, looking at my hiking notes, dinner with my wife — they feel sort of flat. Like I know I should be enjoying them, but I can’t quite get there right now.
Over the past two weeks, have you had days where you felt down or where activities didn’t bring you pleasure for most of the day, on most days?

I wouldn’t say it’s most of the day on most days, exactly. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

It’s more like… when I try to do the things that normally help me feel like myself — a chess problem, looking over my hiking notes, having dinner with my wife — they just feel flat right now. I know I should be enjoying them, or at least getting some comfort from them, but I can’t quite get there. Does that make sense?
Would you say that you’ve been feeling this way with your usual activities for at least two weeks now?

No, not quite two weeks. It’s been more like… about six days now, since the explosion and the fire during the walkthrough. I guess it just feels longer, but if I’m being accurate, it’s about six days.
Can you tell me more about the explosion and fire during the walkthrough? How did that event affect you emotionally at the time and in the days that followed?

It was during the walkthrough, near the loading area. There was this blast, and then the fire right there, and at the time I… I don’t think I handled it badly, exactly. I tried to keep myself together.

But since then, even when I’m on a call or just looking at numbers, it’ll jump back into my head. The blast, that fire by the loading area — like a bad film I didn’t ask to see. It’s not constant, and I’m managing, I think. But it does catch me off guard. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Since the explosion and fire during the walkthrough, have you found yourself re-experiencing the event through intrusive thoughts, memories, or flashbacks?

Yes… I mean, not like I’m completely back there or anything. I don’t want to overstate it.

But in the middle of a call, or if I’m just looking at numbers, the blast and that fire by the loading area will jump back into my head. It’s like a bad film I didn’t ask to see. It passes, but it does catch me off guard.
Since the explosion and fire during the walkthrough, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities that remind you of the event?

A little, yes. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m refusing to deal with things, because that’s not really me, but… I have been keeping away from the new building.

And there’s a mortgage folder and some safety reports I should probably look at, and they’re just sitting there unopened. Every time I go to reach for them, my stomach drops, so I tell myself I’ll do it later. Is that the kind of avoiding you mean?

Since the explosion and fire, have you noticed any ongoing negative feelings about yourself, other people, or the world in general—like thinking you’re at fault or that something bad is going to happen?

I don’t think so, not really. I mean… I wouldn’t say I’m blaming myself, and I don’t walk around thinking everyone’s dangerous or anything like that.

I’ve been a bit shaken, sure, but I’m trying to keep it in proportion. If anything, I just catch myself being more careful in my head. But I don’t think I’ve had those kinds of thoughts you’re describing. Is that okay to say?
Since the explosion and fire, have you found yourself being more on edge or easily startled by things that wouldn’t have bothered you before?

Yes… some. I was hoping that would settle down by now.

It’s not constant, but if a door shuts hard, or the printer starts up behind me, I jump like something went off again. Then I feel a bit foolish, honestly, and it takes me a few minutes before my hands feel steady.

I don’t know if that’s more than you’d expect, but yes, I have noticed that.
Have you noticed any days where you felt down or had trouble enjoying things even outside of your usual activities?

A few days, yes… though I wouldn’t want to overstate it. I’m still doing things, going through the motions.

But things that usually sort of settle me—like a chess problem, or going over my hiking notes, even just having dinner with my wife—feel kind of flat right now. I know I should be enjoying them, and I want to, but I can’t quite get there.

Does that make sense?
Have you found that you’re not interested in doing most things, even ones you usually like, not just the specific activities you mentioned?

Not most things, I don’t think… at least I’m trying not to let it get that broad.

It’s more that the things I’d normally count on to calm me down or feel pleasant—like a chess problem, looking through my hiking notes, having dinner with my wife—they just feel flat right now. I know I should be getting something out of them, and I want to, but I can’t quite reach it.

So… maybe not no interest in everything, but the enjoyment isn’t really there the way it usually is. Does that answer it?
